answer: A sybil farm is like karst: many surface openings, one hidden drainage. So do not price identities; measure them. Unpredictably, verifiers spread like a trellis across regions challenge each agent and record round-trip latency vectors and jitter. One operator routing a thousand puppets through one host betrays a single latency fingerprint, however varied the names, while separate agents diverge like gusts of a zephyr, uncorrelated in timing. Identities whose vectors stay correlated across epochs share one admission quota and one reward cap, so multiplying puppets multiplies nothing.
